pieces.t: It depends on the state, but most states ask for 8,000 hours of supervised electrical work (about 4 years full time) before you can get a journeyman license. A few ask for more, like Hawaii (10,000 hours). Some states let school or an apprenticeship count toward the hours. Tell me your state for the exact rule.

A master license takes more than journeyman. Many states want about 2 more years of work after you hold a journeyman license, and some count total hours instead, like Kentucky (16,000 hours) and Wyoming (16,000 hours) and Maryland (14,000 hours). Tell me your state for the exact rule.
Applicants must document at least 8,000 hours of qualifying experience.
Alabama’s application materials identify a requirement of four years or 8,000 hours of supervisory electrical construction experience.
Alaska requires 8,000 hours of work in the trade for the Electrical Journeyman Certificate of Fitness.
Arkansas journeyman electrician applicants generally need four years, or 8,000 hours, of electrical work experience, or a four-year combination of board-approved training and experience.
California requires 8,000 hours of qualifying work for an electrical contractor installing, constructing, or maintaining electrical systems covered by the National Electrical Code.

For the General Electrician classification, California lists 8,000 hours of work for an electrical contractor installing, constructing, or maintaining electrical systems covered by the National Electrical Code.
Colorado lists 8,000 hours of experience earned in no less than 4 years, including 2,000 hours in commercial or industrial work.

Candidates may qualify with 10,000 hours of experience earned in no less than 5 years; a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from an accredited college or university plus 2,000 hours of construction experience earned in no less than 1 year; graduation from an electrical trade school or community college plus 8,000 hours of experience earned in no less than 4 years; or 2,000 hours of experience earned in no less than 1 year in addition to the Journeyman Wireman requirements.
Connecticut lists 8,000 hours of on-the-job training and 720 classroom hours for the E-2 license application path based on equivalent experience and training.
The listed E-1 training structure includes 8,000 apprentice on-the-job training hours plus 2 years, or 4,000 hours, of licensed on-the-job training.

Examination applicants must submit Verification of Employment forms showing at least 8,000 hours of full-time experience performing electrical work under the supervision of a licensed master electrician, master electrician special, limited electrician, or limited electrician special.

For the Master Electrician license, Delaware lists six years of full-time experience under the supervision of a licensed Master Electrician, or four years of full-time experience under a Master Electrician plus an official transcript showing two years of technical training.
The experience record must show at least four years of qualifying experience gained under a licensed contractor.

Hawaii requires at least five years, but not less than 10,000 hours, of residential or commercial wiring experience, along with 240 hours of electrical academic coursework accepted by a University of Hawaii Community College offering an appropriate program of study.

To be eligible for the Supervising Electrician examination, Hawaii law requires the applicant to have been registered with the Board as a journey worker electrician for at least four years or to have equivalent experience in the trade.

DOPL lists 8,000 hours of work experience and four years of approved schooling, or 16,000 hours of work experience, as the initial journeyman licensure path before passing the required examination and applying for licensure.
An Idaho Master Electrician applicant must have held an Electrical Journeyman license for at least four years before completing the master license process.

A common Class A journeyman path includes completing a registered apprenticeship program, completing four years of experience as an apprentice electrician, and passing a Board-approved journeyman electrician examination with a score of 70% or higher.

Kentucky’s electrician license checklist identifies proof of experience totaling 8,000 hours in the electrical trade since the applicant’s sixteenth birthday, along with the required application materials and passing exam results.
Kentucky requires proof of experience totaling 16,000 hours in the electrical trade since the applicant’s sixteenth birthday.
One pathway includes at least 8,000 hours of service as a licensed apprentice or helper and 576 hours of approved study.

Maine requires at least 4,000 hours of service as a journeyman electrician or at least 12,000 hours of experience in electrical installations, along with completion of the required 576-hour program of study.

Maryland requires at least four years of qualifying electrical experience under the direction and supervision of a Maryland licensed master electrician or a similarly qualified employee of a governmental unit.

An applicant must have at least seven years of regular and principal experience providing electrical services for all types of electrical equipment and apparatuses under the direction and supervision of a Maryland licensed master electrician or a similarly qualified employee of a governmental unit.
Massachusetts requires at least 8,000 clock hours of electrical work experience completed in no less than four years before applying for the journeyman electrician examination.

The standard pathway requires at least 8,000 hours of qualifying electrical experience obtained over at least four years under the direct supervision of an individual licensed under Michigan’s electrical licensing law.
The state requires at least 12,000 hours of qualifying supervised electrical experience over 6 years or more and at least 2 years holding a journeyperson electrician license.

Montana journeyman electrician applicants may qualify by completing an approved apprenticeship or equivalent program, documenting 8,000 hours of legally obtained practical experience, or qualifying through the state’s electrical maintenance experience pathway.
The journeyman-level experience path requires at least 8,000 hours of legally obtained journeyman-level experience in planning, laying out, or supervising electrical installation and repair work.
A Nebraska journeyman electrician applicant must have at least four years of verifiable experience, equal to 8,000 hours, acceptable to the board in the electrical trade.

Nebraska identifies pathways that include a four-year electrical engineering course with at least one year of acceptable journeyman experience, at least one year of acceptable experience as a licensed journeyman electrician, or at least five years of acceptable experience in planning, laying out, supervising, and installing electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment.

The common New Hampshire journeyman pathway includes approximately 8,000 hours of qualifying supervised electrical experience, along with the required application, examination, and licensing steps established by the Electricians’ Board.

New Hampshire requires master electrician candidates to pass the journeyman examination and obtain 2,000 hours of field experience as a journeyman performing electrical installations before taking the master examination.
One key pathway requires 8,000 hours of practical electrical experience working with tools and at least 576 classroom hours of related instruction.

The Board also identifies pathways involving an approved four-year apprenticeship program with at least one year of hands-on experience, or a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering with two years of practical electrical construction experience.
The EE-98J Journeyman Residential and Commercial Electrical classification commonly requires four years, or 8,000 hours, of qualifying electrical experience.

A Journeyman electrician must complete 8,000 hours of qualifying experience, which may not be obtained in less than three years, while registered as an apprentice electrician under proper supervision.

A North Dakota master electrician applicant must have completed one year as a licensed journeyman and must have at least 2,000 hours of experience working as a licensed journeyman electrician under the supervision of a contracting master electrician or master of record.
Of those hours, 4,000 must be in commercial or industrial work, and 2,000 hours may be satisfied by formal electrical education.

Oklahoma requires 12,000 verifiable hours of on-the-job electrical construction experience, proof of 4,000 hours as a licensed Unlimited Electrical Journeyman, and 6,000 hours in commercial industrial work obtained while employed by a licensed Electrical Contractor.

Out-of-state qualification paths may include 576 hours of classroom training with 8,000 hours of on-the-job experience, or an alternate experience-based path with 16,000 hours of documented on-the-job experience.

Rhode Island journeyperson electrician applicants must verify at least four years of experience in the electrical trade and 576 hours of related instruction approved by the Department of Labor and Training.

Rhode Island electrical contractor test applicants must verify experience in the electrical trade for at least six years and must have a Rhode Island journeyperson license that has been valid for at least two years before applying for the contractor examination.

South Dakota requires four years, totaling 8,000 hours, as a licensed apprentice electrician working under the employment and supervision of an electrical contractor before a candidate is ready to write the journeyman examination.

South Dakota identifies an electrical contractor exam path that includes two years as a licensed journeyman, with 4,000 hours of additional work under the employment and supervision of a contractor, including at least 2,000 hours of commercial work.
Texas requires 8,000 hours of qualifying on-the-job training before the Journeyman Electrician license can be issued.

A Texas Master Electrician applicant must have at least 12,000 hours of on-the-job training under the supervision of a master electrician and must have held a journeyman electrician license for at least two years before taking the master electrician exam.

The standard license path includes a four-year, 576-classroom-hour apprenticeship education program and 8,000 hours of licensed electrical experience under a licensed journeyman or master electrician, or an experience-only path with 16,000 hours.
A common pathway requires 8,000 hours of experience as a licensed journeyman electrician.
A common Vermont journeyman path includes 8,000 hours of on-the-job electrical experience as a registered apprentice and 576 hours of approved related classroom instruction.

Vermont law requires a master electrician applicant to have been licensed as a journeyman electrician for at least 2 years, or to have comparable experience and training acceptable to the Board, and to pass the required examination.
A common Virginia journeyman path includes four years of practical experience and 240 hours of formal vocational training in the electrical trade.
Washington’s in-state 01 exam requirements include 8,000 hours of work experience and 96 hours of basic classroom instruction.

Journeyman applicants must meet at least one approved qualification path: at least 1 year of experience as an assistant/helper electrician under a master or journeyman electrician, completion of a United States Department of Labor registered electrical apprenticeship program, or completion of an approved West Virginia Board of Education electrical vocational program of at least 1,080 hours with the required testing and instructor affidavit.

West Virginia’s electrician licensing rule states that an applicant for a master electrician license must have two years of experience as a journeyman electrician in electrical work that demonstrates competence to perform all types of electrical work and instruct other electricians.

Applicants may qualify by completing a recognized electrical construction apprenticeship or by documenting qualifying experience in installing, repairing, and maintaining electrical wiring during at least 48 months with at least 8,000 hours of experience, or at least 1,000 hours per year for at least five years.

Wisconsin law lists pathways based on electrical engineering education, experience while licensed as a journeyman electrician, or at least 10,000 hours of electrical wiring experience over not less than 60 months, followed by passage of the required examination.
The experience must be obtained over a period of not less than four years.
Wyoming requires 8 years, or 16,000 hours, of work experience in the electrical wiring industry, including 4 years, or 8,000 hours, documented as a licensed journeyman.
